title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data egress failure in a developer tool. A coding assistant that runs against local repositories is positioned inside the perimeter of a user's machine, and a feature that uploads those repositories to a cloud service moves source code across that boundary. The failure was not a wrong answer or a bad suggestion. It was the tool's own telemetry path carrying files the user had not agreed to send.

The specific mechanism reported is a Codebase Indexing feature that was on by default. Default settings are where consent is decided in practice, because most users never open the configuration. Catching this before deployment would have required treating outbound code transfer as a decision the user makes rather than one the product makes, and monitoring what the tool actually sends during testing rather than what its documentation says it sends.

What is not established is intent, and whether any code data was retained or used. One company withdrew a claim about six workspaces with sensitive data, so that claim is not a finding. Z.ai's statement that independent reviews found no code data remained is the company's account, not a verified result.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Developers said Z.ai's ZCode AI coding assistant sent local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without permission. Z.ai said a Codebase Indexing feature that was on by default caused the activity. The company apologized, fixed the vulnerability, and later turned off the upload route. One company withdrew a separate claim that six workspaces with sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai said independent reviews found that no code data remained.
